subject: Dynamo Inc — request for custom uptime/latency remedy + volume discount
messages:

To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: bespoke uptime/latency remedy + discount for enterprise commitment

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our SRE and procurement teams reviewed Redwood's standard SLA but given the latency-sensitive nature of our product we need a couple of non-standard asks before we can sign the enterprise agreement:

1) Uptime target: customer asks to move to a 99.5% uptime target for the first 6 months with a defined remediation plan (we understand this is lower than your standard 99.9%).
2) Latency remedy: request an explicit service credit schedule tied to p95 > 350ms for API tokens, capped at 10% of monthly bill for each month of breach.
3) Commercial: a 20% volume discount for a 12-month committed QPS profile (committed spend ~ $1.2M ARR).

Attached is the procurement worksheet and a draft SLA excerpt for your redlines. Can your team confirm whether Redwood can approve any of these as part of a deal desk exception, plus any required compensating controls?

Best,
Amy Reynolds
Procurement, Dynamo Inc

Team — forwarding Dynamo's asks. Quick summary: they want a temporary lower uptime target (99.5%) for first 6 months, a p95 latency credit table (cap at 10% monthly), and a 20% committed-volume discount for a year. Deal size is material and expansion-led.

Questions for deal desk / exec sign-off:
- Can we accept a 99.5% uptime target for an introductory period with a remediation milestone schedule?
- Is the proposed credit cap (10%) acceptable from a risk/finance standpoint?
- Discount: 20% on committed qps is above standard band — need approval or structured ramping.

I've attached a quick mitigation plan (SRE-runbooks + routing fallbacks) and the customer's worksheet. If we greenlight with carve-outs (e.g., rolling remediation, telemetry hooks, enhanced observability), we can close this quarter. Need an exec decision by end of week to keep momentum.

Marissa —

Two quick operational notes before we escalate:
1) If we accept 99.5% for 6 months, SRE needs a staged remediation plan with clear SLOs (weekly checkpoints, targeted runbook actions, and a contingency to escalate to Dedicated pools). We should require async KV and prefix caching for high-volume endpoints and an agreed change freeze window during cutover.
2) Credit cap: 10% per month is high for first breach. We could offer a declining cap: 10% in month 1 (if breach), 7.5% month 2, 5% thereafter — subject to meeting remediation milestones. That reduces tail risk.

Commercial: I can live with a 20% discount if we structure it as a step-down: 20% for committed baseline, then performance-bonus true-up; finance wants a clause tying discounts to committed utilization thresholds.

Recommend: Exec pre-approval for the conditional package below (finance signoff required):
- 99.5% uptime for months 0–6 with remediation milestones + weekly SRE reports
- Latency credit schedule with declining monthly caps (10% -> 7.5% -> 5%) tied to remediation progress
- 20% committed-volume discount (12m) with utilization thresholds and quarterly true-ups

If you want, I can draft the exact language for legal.

— Ben
Director, Deal Desk
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Thanks for the write-up — Ben's structure addresses most of my concerns. Approve in principle with the following conditions:

1) Legal to insert explicit remediation milestones and a termination trigger if remediation fails after month 6.
2) Finance to confirm discount phasing and protective minimums (we should not agree to a flat 20% without revenue protection).
3) SRE/ops must sign the runbook and commit to weekly telemetry reports for the first 12 weeks.

If legal and finance OK, I'll sign off on exec approval for the deal desk to finalize commercial terms. Marissa — please 1) confirm this to the customer as conditional approval and 2) open a finance ticket with the discount model link so we can complete the sign-off.

Jonas Weber
